title: The Mercy of the Creator and the Judgment of the Shepherds
english: For they are not slaughtered by the lawless overseers for any other reason or to be eaten, regarding which it is said, 'If men rise up against us, then they would have eaten us alive' (Ps 116:6). But they failed in their murderous haste to say graciously, like those who were rescued, 'Blessed is the Lord, who did not give us into the trap of those pursuing Him' (Ps 116:6).

Those who think they are owners and not shepherds of the flocks entrusted to them, slaughtering the sheep with a knife—and this is their sophistical discourse, proclaiming impious attitudes—did not regret or repent for what they acted in robbery and murder. For they carelessly sell those things which are not their own as if they were theirs, and with shameless audacity they shout that they have grown rich, while those who strive to please the one who deems the All-King to be the shepherd of the flock do not slaughter nor prevent those which the sheep logically entrusted, so that they might unjustly grow rich from greed and shameful gains.

In order that such a thing might not happen through the inattention of the overseers of the Church, the proclaimer of the apostles, Peter, cries out, thus writing: 'I exhort the elders among you to shepherd the flock that is among you, not by compulsion but willingly, not exercising dominion over the appointed ones, so that, when the Chief Shepherd, Christ Jesus, is revealed, you may receive the unfading crown of glory' (1 Pet 5:2-4); meaning those who exercise dominion, namely the sheep of Christ, while the negligent shepherds are acting, selling for shameful gains the divine flocks so that they shout, 'We have grown rich,' devouring those whom they lift up through scandals.

Thus, having harmed and done evil to the peoples, the sheep allegorically called, their false shepherds suffered nothing from them, not sympathizing with the flock according to the one saying: 'Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is stumbled, and I am not burned?' (Rom 15:1). Into this love the divine instructors are led by the Savior becoming a pattern for them, as the God-wise Evangelist John calls out to those who worship God according to Christ: 'That He,' clearly that Christ, 'set His soul as a ransom for us, and we owe to lay down our souls for one another' (1 John 3:16).
Those having such a mind toward those who embrace the same and think the same, being brothers sympathetic, [to] those slaughtering the...

The sheep handed over to them oppose those who speak with insolence, saying: 'We have become rich; we have acquired sheep through shameful gain, and having devoured them, we suffer very little because of them.' (Zach. XI, 6–7: 'Therefore I will no longer spare those inhabiting the land, says the Lord, and behold, I am handing over men every man to the hand of his neighbor and to the hand of his king, and they shall cut down the land, and I will by no means come out of their hand.' And I shepherd the sheep of the slaughter toward Canaan.)

Since those entrusted with the care of the logical sheep despised them, neither sympathizing with nor caring for their salvation, but selling them to strangers through shameful gain, the Lord Almighty threatens no longer to spare the land, that is, those dwelling upon it, handing over the weaker ones to the tyrants through whom they suppose to have strength and brutality, so that all those upon the land may be cut down, handing over every man into the hands of his neighbor and into the hands of his king, no longer by lawful means but by tyrannical rule.

God repeats these things in the manner of a threat, so that those toward whom the threat is directed may cease from sinning through the fear of what is expected. For God never fails his own works, as the all-virtuous Wisdom of Solomon says: 'Spare all, O Despot, soul-loving one, loathing nothing of what you have made, for you did not fashion anything in hatred.' 'For you created for the sake of being, and the generations of the world are salvific.'

Having experience of this exceeding goodness of Him who has composed all things and provides for all things, those who serve Him bring a petition on behalf of the people, saying: 'Spare, Lord, your people, and do not give your inheritance to the ruin of the nations that will begin to prevail over them, lest the nations say: Where is their God?'
To such an extent did the Cause and Guardian of all spare the race of men, as to give His Son as a ransom for all, into death, so that He might redeem those dying by reigning over death.
The Apostle, becoming a mystagogue of this exceeding salvation, writes concerning God: 'He who did not spare His own Son, but delivered Him up for us...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Two Rods and the One Shepherd
english: Him—how will He not also grant all things with Him to us? Sparing us, He did not withhold the Son; for He is impassible and the destroyer of all harm, but we are mortals and subject to passions. Therefore, if He had been sparing of the Son, not having given Him up to 'taste death for all' (Hebrews 2:9), we would have remained in the ruin that holds fast through the transgression of the divine commandment; but so that we might be set free, the guardian gave up His own Son, not to be harmed by dying, having been revealed as Savior, having been given up for them.

Having these things thus, if God says: 'I will no longer spare those dwelling on the earth,' He admonishes by the fear of threat, so that they might not fall by being executed, but might come out of the sin that holds fast, no longer being subject to execution. He makes manifest the manner of not sparing anymore, saying 'to deliver men into the hands of their neighbors and into the hands' of the 'evil king whom they chose, so that the earth might be cut off' (Isaiah 17:1), as they oppose one another as 'men who are dying.' These are those walking according to the flesh in strife and jealousy. Men who are such are delivered into the hands of those whom they had as neighbors, [namely] demons, through greed and material disposition. For then they are most able to be admonished, having been delivered to those whom they thought were friends and neighbors, having been tested by their coarseness and ferocity; and they will flee also from the one who rules tyrannically, having experienced his hardness. For even the people of the Hebrews desired in such a way to be set free from the insolence of the Egyptians, having known their turbulence and their lawless dominion.

When the earth is cut off, that is, when those upon it are revolting, God shepherds the sheep of the slaughter into Canaan, the prepared punishment. It was also said previously that the sheep of the slaughter are those ready to suffer and those already slaughtered, when we received that which was being reported by the afflicted to the Benefactor of all: 'You gave us as sheep for eating' (Psalm 50:5), and again: 'We were counted as sheep for slaughter' (Psalm 50:6). Understand whether the shepherding of the sheep of the slaughter into Canaan denotes something praiseworthy, being interpreted as the prepared [place], perhaps of those being led in through being managed by harm.

Working out an unchangeable salvation through pains brought on pedagogically, about which the law-giving apostle Paul writes, marking these things: 'The godly sorrow works out unchangeable repentance unto salvation, bringing about the death of the sorrow of the world' (2 Cor 7:10). Therefore, this [worldly sorrow] must be rejected, but the godly one must be unchangeably opposed, bringing about salvation according to God.

4.71 Zechariah 11:7: 'And I will take for myself two rods—the one I called Beauty, and the other I called Union—and I will shepherd the sheep. And I will separate the three shepherds in one month, and my soul will be burdened by them, for their souls were pressing upon me. And I said, I will not shepherd you.' 4.72 From the person of the Savior, the prophet Zechariah 11:21 announces the things concerning the two rods which he had taken for himself.

4.73 Nothing else is signified in the passages concerning the rods except a scepter of rule, rather a symbol of kingship. 4.74 Since therefore the whole human race is divided into the people from the circumcision and into the Church called from the Gentiles, the God of the Jews and the Gentiles, being both Savior and King of them, took for himself the two scepters, so that from both he might work out one kingship.

4.75 And the prophecy will be understood from the evangelical utterance; for just as one kingship was shown under one king from those having believed among the Gentiles and the Jews, so also one flock is shown under one shepherd, the true one, who has set his soul down for the sheep. Thus the evangelical voice is announced by the Savior: 'And I have other sheep which are not of this fold; them also I must bring together, and they will hear my voice, so that there will become one flock and one shepherd' (John 10:16), saying that the other sheep are to be those from the Gentiles believing in the Gospel, not from the Jewish fold.

4.76 It is the same thing, the two flocks becoming under one shepherd, as it is the two scepters coming under the same king. But when will this be fulfilled? Perhaps when it happens: 'Rejoice, O nations, with his people' (Zech 9:7)? 4.77 And it is also said differently: 'And I have other sheep which are not of this fold,' the fold being called that of the sheep of this earthly world in which those bearing the body are wearing out [their lives], being delivered...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Three False Shepherds and the Soul
english: These souls, having dwelt in the underworld until now, are gathered just as the good shepherd gathers them, having come to them when he 'died for all' in order that 'he might rule over the living and the dead.' If one rules the living and the dead with royal power and pastoral knowledge, the two flocks and kingdoms have been shown to be one.

When this has been established, the polyarchy will be destroyed, as the true shepherd removes the bad rulers—three shepherds in one month, that is, in one single cycle. These three removed leaders are to be considered: the Jewish priestly order, those called unjust prophets by them, and those who reigned from Jeroboam. For all these were causes of harm among those who were ruling. It has been said in Hosea: 'Priests have hidden the way of the Lord, Sicaim has murdered, they have done iniquity in Israel' (Hosea 4:6), and even in the same prophet: 'Israel shall be afflicted like the prophet who went astray' (Hosea 4:12).

Many things are written regarding the unlawful kingship that split God's people, such as: 'Hear this, O priests, and house of the king, be appalled, because the judgment is against you, that you have become a snare to the vision, and like a net spread out over the Sea of Tiberias' (Habakkuk 3:8/Amos 8:1-2). Against those who thought so poorly, the holy Jeremiah cries out most strictly from the presence of the All-King God: 'The priests did not say, Where is the Lord? and those upholding the law did not seek me, and the prophets prophesied unjustly, and the shepherds were ungodly toward me, and they followed after unprofitable things' (Jeremiah 2:11).

Understand that the kings of Israel, besides the priests and prophets, were also found to be ungodly shepherds toward Him. Also, the false teachers should not be ignored, who claim to be ungodly shepherds toward God. These three called shepherds are removed in one month by 'the great High Priest Jesus, having opened the heavens,' being a true prophet, concerning whom a divine pre-announcement was said: 'The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brothers' (Deuteronomy 18:15). To be both high priest and prophet, and also king, is as it is said concerning the Father: 'I have raised him up as king...'

And all his ways are straight; he will build my city, and will return the captivity of my people, not with ransoms nor with gifts (Isa 54:17; Isa 60:14). And he himself, the one building the spiritual city of God and redeeming the people, says about himself: 'I have been made king by him upon the holy Mount Zion, I proclaim the command of the Lord' (Isa 62:6).

Regarding the things observed concerning the three shepherds, it is necessary to oversee that three false ones are to be considered as shepherds, the impious ones being removed who are impious toward the Trinity. For some of them have much inclination toward being impious toward the Father, others toward the Son, and others toward the Holy Spirit.

And perhaps those thinking [the Father is] the father of the Son are blaspheming toward the Father, diminishing the Father because of their impiety toward the Only-begotten Son, who is the God Word of wisdom and truth, those who were previously thinking [him] to be a creature from non-being and blaspheming concerning his own offspring. And they are also fighting against the Spirit, glorifying [him] as if he were one of the creatures.
And the three ranks of the deceived atheists think [wrongly] concerning the Trinity, but each, as has already been said, has a different impious inclination.

And the impious shepherds in this way will be uprooted in one month; for until the present age, the false teaching holds the promise, to be destroyed when a perfect illumination of the true light occurs after the present evil age and the transient life, upon which alone those hoping are more merciful than all men.

And the uprooting of the three wicked leaders happens, under the heavy law falling upon them of the king who threatens these things, since they do hateful things to him. And his soul is said to be characterized in several ways.

According to one, and an easy one, it is that which he has as a perfect man, which he sets aside in order to receive it again. He has indeed set it as a ransom, having given it instead of many, as the mystagogue of the truth, John, writes about him thus: 'Because he laid down his soul for us; and we owe to lay down our souls for one another' (Eph 5:2); and having risen from the dead, he received it, 'not having been left in Hades' (John 14:18). According to another view, the soul is every man having been made to belong to this Savior who says these things.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
